newsitem.title: INDIA: Foreign funds can invest in India gilts - RBI.
newsitem.headline: Foreign funds can invest in India gilts - RBI.

text.p: India's central bank on Saturday said foreign institutional investors (FIIs) can invest in all dated government securities except treasury bills.
The announcement followed a government decision in January to allow foreign funds to invest in government securities, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said in its guidelines.
Treasury bills are for shorter maturities of less than a year while other government securities mature over many years.
The securities can be bought at auctions or floatations and from the secondary market, the RBI said.
The FIIs will be allowed entry only through subsidiary general ledger (SGL) account through designated banks.

Secondary market transactions will be permitted through stock markets or over-the-counter with SGL account holders and will be governed by the RBI's delivery versus payment settlement system, the central bank added.
